correctness.rationale: On f_k=0 only the kth summand survives and the angle speed is A_k times positive factors for r<1/2. The center A_k are positive; the gradients sum to zero, canceling degree six. At y=0 only the third summand contributes to the first component, whose fifth-degree coefficient is −√3/20. The transverse variable f_k gives the physical-time cofactor integral: 2det(z−C_i,z−C_k)=−∂θf_i. The constant ratio term integrates to zero; the linear ratio term paired with 2r d·Je/|d|² produces the stated negative r² coefficients (each S_k>0), with a uniform O(r³) remainder. For the quartic normal form, one can independently restrict to each complexified circle using ζ=(x+iy)−c_k and (x−iy)−conj(c_k)=r²/ζ. The two tangent component expressions force the scalar angular coefficient to have Laurent exponents −3,…,3. Pairwise intersections are transverse, with no triple point for r<1/2, so that coefficient vanishes at the two intersections with each other circle. Dividing by f_j f_l leaves exponents −1,…,1, hence an affine real B_k. The polynomial residual is f_1f_2f_3 times a constant vector, forced to vanish by the degree-six terms, which also give Σ∇B_i=0. At degree five, writing G=Σ C_i(∇B_i)^⊤, the vector identity forces det(z,Gz)=0, so G=cI, and ΣB_i(0)=−c. With c=κ√3/2 these are exactly the listed coefficients. On circle 1, reflection swaps f_2 and f_3 and their coefficients for b_2=b_3. Varying b_3−b_2 at fixed b_1 and κ gives the derivative of log(f_2/f_3) divided by 2B_1. In the bisector angle this derivative is 2r(w−2rv)/Q; subtracting the constant reciprocal at w=2rv yields one strict signed integral, proportional to sign κ. Physical-time orientation multiplies by sign b_1. Rotating gives the two cyclic counterparts. If two b coincide or κ=0 there is a zero exponent; otherwise common sign of the three exponents would force the two extreme b values to have one sign and the median the opposite, impossible. This rules out three hyperbolic attractors at degree ≤4; negation reverses hyperbolic stability. The supplied symbolic checker was inspected, not run; the proofs establish the degree bound and the uniform small-radius statement without it.
